Looking for an exercise that targets a specific movement.

There's no one specific movement. Lots of work for the glutes, hamstrings, hip flexors, abs and lower back would be needed. Hanging leg raises, glute-ham raises, superman pushups, lying bridge curls, and pistol squats could all be used. You'd also probably want to build your calves, to increase the overall mass of your leg [F=ma] and to provide some shock absorption in case you miss the kick and hit higher up on your leg. So throw in some calf raises or one-leg hop runs.

You said it yourself; inverted straight leg raises; get on a handstand (a headstand would probably not allow enough room) against a wall, and move the legs up and down; add ankle weights if the movement is too easy. You might also want to supplement with flexibility work to get the full range you want (but remember that more flexibility than what you need is not a good thing). Doing it one leg at a time might also help to get the desired range and place less stress on your lower back, at the cost of more time.

You also have to practice the target movement itself, as even if your strength and power go up by only doing inverted leg raises, your performance at the movement will decrease a bit in the absence of specific training.
